reason: The storm may cut solar power, so connecting the charged reserve seems like a practical first step toward the shutdown.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to its emergency power supply, though other shutdown steps may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Moving the heat store would help protect the garden, but securing reserve power seems more urgent.
The outdoor line will lose heat, so its shutdown matters too; I chose to address the power supply first.

effect: The reserve now powers essential loads, but garden circulation is off, so the beds need protection in the nook.
reaction: The dimming lights and stopped circulation make the storm feel immediate.
reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so addressing it at the shutdown controls seems useful before moving the garden.
expectation: I expect the line to be isolated or otherwise prepared for the loss of heat, though I don't know exactly how.

alternatives.reason: The heat store could warm the sheltered garden, but the exposed water line also needs attention.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, with its pump and thaw checks on reserve power. The next goal is to move both troughs and the heat store into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line makes the shutdown feel more concrete; I’m curious how the garden will be kept circulating.
reason: The heat store can provide warmth in the sheltered nook, so I’ll move it there first.
expectation: I expect the charged tank to be placed inside the nook, where it can slowly release heat around the beds.

alternatives.reason: The lettuce also needs shelter, but I want the heat source in place first.
The potato trough needs shelter too, but the heat store seems useful to both beds.

effect: The heat store is in the nook, where it will soften the initial cold while reserve power supplies longer-term heating. Both troughs still need to be moved.
reaction: The distinction between stored warmth and longer-term heating makes the shelter plan clearer.
reason: The lettuce needs shelter, and moving it into the warmed nook advances the current goal.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the nook; the potato trough will still need to follow.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs shelter, but I have no clear reason to move it before the lettuce.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and the potato trough still needs to be moved.
reaction: Carrying the bed level and protecting its leaves makes the move feel tangible.
reason: Moving the potato trough is the only available combination and completes the current move into the nook.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be sheltered alongside the lettuce and heat store, though further steps may be needed to keep both beds going.

effect: Both troughs and the heat store are now sheltered in the nook, completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: The attention to the potato bed’s cover, support and leaves made the move feel concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Moving the heat store was most worthwhile: it clarified how stored warmth cushions the first cold hours while reserve power provides longer-term heating.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the two troughs felt somewhat repetitive, although the details of their different shapes and fittings helped distinguish them.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the shutdown drained the outdoor line while keeping its pump and thaw checks on essential power.

arbitrary.text: The order of moving the two troughs felt arbitrary; I had no clear reason to choose lettuce first.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to see how the station and garden fare through the storm and what Earth learns from the specimens.
